IESC is an execution/integration candidate rather than a pure equipment manufacturer; survival into later layers requires proof that custom engineered solutions are tied to switchgear, power modules, substations, or interconnection work.

PLPC is a second-order grid/substation hardware candidate with low AI mindshare; later layers should test whether utility capex in data-center-heavy regions is converting into identifiable order growth.
Eaton should be used as the reference demand validator for Electrical Americas backlog and data-center order acceleration, not as the main underfollowed alpha candidate.

Need a separate materials/components pass for grain-oriented electrical steel, copper busbar, insulation, transformer oil, relays/protection, testing/inspection, and transformer repair/refurbishment companies.
POWL is the highest-confidence direct public-market mapping for the grid_transformers_switchgear node due to explicit medium-voltage switchgear language, record backlog and mega data-center orders.

PLPC should be tracked as an underfollowed second-order grid-hardware candidate, but survival to later layers requires evidence that incremental growth is tied to U.S. utility T&D/substation projects serving data-center load growth.
PPSI is a below-$300M speculative-shadow exception only; require hard data-center customer/order/backlog evidence before promoting beyond Layer 1.

Switchgear, bus systems, control buildings, substation hardware and grid-line components may be better underfollowed hunting zones than obvious transformer OEMs because many are buried in industrial-electrical or infrastructure-product labels.

Need a later pass focused specifically on U.S.-listed or OTC transformer materials and components: grain-oriented electrical steel, copper conductors, insulation, bushings, relays, sensors and testing/inspection providers.

POWL should remain in the grid_transformers_switchgear node as a direct underfollowed-to-mid-attention switchgear/electrical-room candidate; key survival evidence is data-center backlog conversion and repeat orders.

WS is a second-order materials/component candidate for transformer-core and electrical-steel bottlenecks; evidence is weaker than direct equipment suppliers and requires segment/customer verification.
PPSI is below the preferred market-cap range and should be tracked only as a speculative_shadow micro-cap exception until data-center-specific orders or backlog are verified.

Additional Layer 1B searches should test other U.S.-listed niche names around power-quality equipment, protective relays, busbars, electrical enclosures, transformer bushings/insulation, and substation testing/certification services.
POWL is a high-priority direct node candidate for medium-voltage switchgear and behind-the-meter data-center power gear; monitor whether the >$400M data-center order repeats.

IESC maps to the execution-capacity chokepoint: electrical installation, data-center communications infrastructure, custom engineered solutions, and field services rather than transformer manufacturing.
PLPC adds an adjacent substation/T&D hardware layer that may benefit from grid interconnection and utility upgrade activity caused by data-center load growth.

Further Layer 1C/2 searches should test component vendors below the obvious OEMs: busbar systems, electrical steel/GOES, transformer insulation, bushings, protection relays, breakers, and commissioning/testing providers.

summary: Combined focused Layer 1B searches: Expanded the direct public-company universe for the transformer/switchgear/substation node using a two-lane Serenity funnel. Reference lane: Eaton as the obvious large electrical-equipment validator. Underfollowed lane: Powell Industries for medium-voltage switchgear and packaged power systems, IES Holdings for electrical/data-center infrastructure execution and custom engineered solutions, and Preformed Line Products for grid/substation hardware that can benefit one step away from the obvious AI data-center buildout. This is research support only, not a buy/sell recommendation. Expanded the universe around U.S. AI/data-center power-infrastructure chokepoints using a two-lane funnel. Reference lane: larger electrical-equipment names validating demand in switchgear, bus systems, utility T&D and data-center electrical infrastructure. Underfollowed lane: more focused or less-obvious public companies tied to custom medium-voltage switchgear, grid-line/substation hardware, and microgrid/mobile-power alternatives. The strongest direct evidence in this pass is Powell Industries' record backlog and explicit mega data-center orders; the best underfollowed second-order evidence is Preformed Line Products' grid/network construction exposure. Pioneer Power is included only as a micro-cap speculative-shadow candidate because its relevance is plausible but requires much stronger order/backlog verification.
